subject: Air-gapped observability: egress strategy, SIEM resilience & trace correlation
messages:
From: Sophia Lee <sophia.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Visibility for our air-gapped Redwood private deploy

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting a locked-down private deployment for a regulated workload and need alignment on observability egress options and compliance evidence. A few specific asks from our security team: 

- Near-real-time SIEM ingest (Splunk preferred) where possible, but must support periods of zero-outbound connectivity (air-gapped).
- Proof of delivery / signed evidence bundles for audit (weekly and ad-hoc).
- Token/certificate rotation and key management policy that meets our SOC2 requirements.
- Trace correlation across the service boundary so our distributed traces remain end-to-end for incident investigations.

Can you outline feasible architectures (HEC over mTLS via a forwarder, pull-based secure sync, offline bundle transfer) and the acceptance criteria we should expect to present to our compliance team? Also include constraints (latency windows, retention, required ports/protocols).

We have a Splunk PS contact copied. Hoping to schedule a short technical workshop this week.

Thanks,
Sophia Lee
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp

Hi Sophia / team,

Looping in Kimberly, Marissa and Ben — internal owners for SIEM acceptance, evidence packaging and on-prem forwarders. Quick summary of proposed approaches and trade-offs below. I've attached a short options doc (airgap-obsv-options-v1.md) for reference.

Summary of feasible patterns (short):
1) Push HEC via an in-customer forwarder (preferred where outbound allowed)
   - Splunk HEC on TLS, client cert + token rotation (mTLS recommended).
   - Near real-time, minimal latency. Requires outbound to Splunk IPs/ports or a Splunk collector in customer VPC.
2) Pull-based secure sync
   - Customer side writes encrypted batches to a restricted S3 (or SFTP) staging location that Redwood pulls through a hardened egress host. Good for strict egress controls; introduces batch delay (minutes-hours).
3) Offline signed evidence bundles
   - For strict air-gapped windows: periodic signed ZIP bundles (SHA256 + server cert signature) transferred via controlled channel (sneaker-net, secure courier, or one-way transfer appliance). Meets strongest audit constraints but is not real-time.

Tradeoffs to call out:
- Latency vs compliance: real-time HEC is best for ops; signed bundles are best for auditability.
- Authentication: token rotation cadence + client certs mitigate token theft in constrained networks.
- Trace correlation: preserve W3C traceparent headers or embed trace IDs in log events at ingress. Ensure consistent timestamping (NTP) and monotonic ID generation to avoid holes in service maps.

Next asks from our side to produce a runbook:
- Confirm whether you can accept mTLS client cert auth to a Splunk HEC endpoint, or require token-only.
- Expected max QPS / events per second so we can size spooling.
- Preferred rotation cadence for tokens/certs.

I'll circulate a runbook draft and an acceptance checklist. Marissa, can you prepare the signed-runbook bundle and the HEC rotation checklist? Ben / Kimberly, please call out any hardened egress host constraints we should avoid.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference

Attachments: airgap-obsv-options-v1.md
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Visibility for our air-gapped Redwood private deploy

Hannah / team — technical constraints and recommendations below. Copying only internal commentary here; I'll include a clean version for the customer once we align.

Technical notes / requirements:
- Splunk HEC over TLS with client certs (mTLS) is the preferred pattern. Use short-lived HEC tokens that are rotated via KMS/HSM-backed automation. Recommend 7-day token rotation default for regulated workloads unless Acme requires shorter.
- If mTLS is not possible, require HEC tokens + signed envelope for batch uploads to preserve non-repudiation.
- Local spooler: implement a file spool with atomic rename and SHA256 manifest per batch. Add bundle signing with an intermediate certificate we control (signed by customer CA).
- Time sync: require NTP reachability to a defined set of servers or a GPS time source. Without synchronized clocks trace correlation and signed timestamps fall apart.
- Trace propagation: preserve W3C traceparent and tracestate headers end-to-end. Where we perform re-ingest (pull model), ensure we preserve the original trace IDs and map them into our service map with tags: customer_id:acme, env:prod, deploy:airgap-1.
- Scale/backpressure: where network is intermittent, use a persistent local queue with size cap and backpressure signals to the runtime. Provide an overflow policy: drop oldest, or escalate to runbook.

Fallbacks and resilience:
- Fallback A: Spool to encrypted local disk + offline signed bundle transfer (weekly or on-demand).
- Fallback B: If TLS egress fails, rotate to SFTP push to a managed jump host (pull by Redwood).

I'll add these items to the runbook checklist. Ben — please validate NAT/proxy port requirements and whether the customer prefers outbound-only TLS to a managed collector in their VPC.

-Kimberly

Subject: Draft runbook + acceptance checklist — air-gapped observability

Hi Sophia / Splunk PS — attached is the first draft of the runbook and the acceptance checklist we discussed. The bundle includes two artifacts: a readable runbook and a technical checklist for Splunk HEC + offline bundle handling.

High-level acceptance criteria (summary):
- Splunk can accept HEC over mTLS OR token-based HEC + signed-batch fallback.
- Evidence bundles must include a manifest.json, SHA256 checksums, and a PKCS7 signature from an agreed intermediate CA.
- Token/cert rotation automation must be demonstrable (demo or logs) and retain rotation history for 90 days.
- Trace IDs preserved (W3C traceparent) with mapping tags for customer and deploy id.
- NTP/time-sync verification in acceptance tests.

Attachments in this email (stubs):
- signed-runbook-acme-obsv-v1.zip (contains: runbook.md, acceptance-checklist.md, sample-manifest.json)
- hec-rotation-checklist.pdf

Please review and confirm:
1) Can Splunk accept mTLS client certificates for HEC with our proposed rotation cadence of 7 days?
2) If not, can Splunk accept token rotation + signed envelope for batch pulls?

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_runbook (runbook working folder), JIRA:SUP-3182 (tracking work).

If these align, let's lock a 60 minute workshop Thu 11/12 to walk the runbook and run a quick acceptance test.

Marissa / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the runbook and the acceptance checklist with our compliance and platform teams. Short answers and a couple clarifying questions: 

- We can accept mTLS for HEC. We will need a short test window to provision and validate client cert chains (we control the customer CA). 7-day rotation is acceptable as a starting point.
- Offline signed bundles are acceptable for maintenance windows where outbound is blocked; need to confirm that the manifest schema matches the fields defined in the runbook (sample-manifest.json).
- Please include example log event shapes for the three highest-volume sources (ingress-proxy, model-runtime, auth) — we need field-level retention requirements.
- Confirm retention windows for logs forwarded to Splunk (90 days hot, 365 days cold) and make sure the runbook has a section that maps Redwood export TTL to Acme retention policy.

We can do the workshop Thu 11/12 at 10am PT. Splunk PS — can you confirm mTLS support and an internal contact for test coordination?

I'll prepare a short compliance checklist to run during the workshop.

Thanks,
Sophia Lee
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp
